messages:
sara: Heads-up — after the warmup/prefetch heuristic rolled at 12:05 UTC we saw a 3x increase in backend qps and user p99 jump. Reverting? :warning:

miguel: digging in... kv-prefix cache miss rate went from 7% -> 62% right after deploy. rough log snippet:
```
miss_rate 0.62 @ 2026-03-15T12:06:10Z
cache_hits 3800
cache_misses 6100
backend_latency_p95 420ms
```

olivia: dashboard https://grafana.redwood/d/ABC123/prefix-cache — p95/p99 lines spike at 12:06, cache service GC count increased, memory churn.

infra-bot: deploy: canary/prefetch-heuristic v3 deployed at 2026-03-15T12:05:18Z (sha: a1b2c3)

lena: I disabled prefix cache on canary-3 at 12:15 UTC but prod still on. command I ran:
```
infractl cache disable --service prefix --env canary-3
```

miguel: root cause looks like keying change + tokenizer length interplay. prefetch now includes tokenized_prefix_len in key; tokenizer update produced different tokenization for a lot of routes => cache key churn. also batching changed, causing more small sequential requests that never hit prefetch window.

ryan: suggested quick fixes:
- revert prefetch key change (pin old keyer)
- add miss-rate circuit breaker in cache client (reject queries to cache if miss-rate > 30% for 1m)
- patch tokenizer to stable mode until we roll new keyer

jena: proposed config for circuit breaker:
```
cache.client.miss_breaker.threshold=0.3
cache.client.miss_breaker.window=60s
cache.client.prefetch.enabled=false  # temp
```

sara: applied temporary rollback of prefetch keyer at 12:28 UTC on prod. monitoring => backend qps down to baseline in ~4m. scheduling postmortem.

infra-bot: action: rollback completed at 2026-03-15T12:28:36Z — prefetch-keyer pinned to v2

lena: follow-ups: add jitter to TTLs to avoid synchronized expiry, pre-warm top-200 routes during deploy, and add per-tenant miss limits to prevent noisy neighbors.

miguel: saved profiler traces and vperf dumps to /mnt/perf/prefetch-2026-03-15/trace-1768604321.tar.gz

sara: postmortem meeting tomorrow 14:00 UTC. tagging @product and @support to make sure SLO impact is logged.
